name: Merida
blurb: Mérida is discussed online as a human-scale city featuring a historic district, local markets, and the Paseo de Montejo. Visitors note tropical savanna weather with warm nights and mention its accessibility via cruise stops and upcoming international events like the 2027 IFPA and SCZI conferences.

positive: Lower cost of living compared to US cities
Fascinating, human-scale city with rich markets and historic sites
Diverse local wildlife including urban parrot species
negative: Extended power outages lasting up to fifteen hours during storms
High utility billing despite unreliable grid infrastructure
Unusual local culinary surprises like cold potato-frosted chicken salad

quotes.text: After October 1st. I have no reason to come back.   I mean Mexico's are not that far away. In Merida, a City approximately the size of Indianapolis cost of living for a middle class lifestyle is 360% cheaper.  If you can't live on $1200 per month you expect too much luxury
Southern Mexico, Mérida, Yucatán. There’s 9 species of parrots that have adapted to the urban environment here. I’ve managed to ID three species around my house.

Mérida sat in the dark for fifteen hours. CFE billed the full monopoly rate anyway, that's the whole business model: collect first, maintain never. A grid that can't survive a storm is still a grid that can print an invoice. The blockades are the itemized complaint the utility refused to read.

One day in Mérida is nowhere near enough. But sometimes that’s all you’ve got.
